business_problem: Marsello needed a flexible data platform for fast-moving omnichannel marketing features, sophisticated segmentation, and constant customer growth.
solution_summary: Marsello built its omnichannel marketing platform on MongoDB Atlas so a small development team could handle highly dynamic retail and hospitality data without being slowed by relational-schema changes. Atlas stores customer, e-commerce, loyalty, email, SMS, and point-of-sale information in a document model that can evolve as the product adds new segmentation logic and campaign features. Running Atlas as a managed service on AWS lets the team focus on product development instead of infrastructure operations while still scaling for growing global demand. That architecture helps Marsello deliver data-driven lifecycle marketing for more than 5,000 businesses, move quickly in changing retail conditions, and generate strong customer ROI.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores customer, campaign, and commerce data for Marsello's omnichannel marketing platform.

data_flow: Point-of-sale, e-commerce, and customer-behavior data is stored in MongoDB Atlas, segmented inside Marsello, and then used to trigger targeted email, SMS, and loyalty campaigns.
business_outcome: Marsello iterates faster, powers targeted lifecycle marketing for 5,000 businesses, and helped retailers see 98% average ROI while driving more than $200 million in revenue.
metrics: Marsello empowers more than 5,000 retail and hospitality businesses in over 170 countries.
Marsello helped its retailers gain an average ROI of 98% and over $200 million in revenue for the company itself.
In 2020, movement restrictions in response to COVID-19 led to an increase in e-commerce, growing its share of global retail sales from 16% to 19% in 2020.
architecture_clues: The document model lets fields vary from document to document and supports constant schema evolution.
Atlas runs as a managed service on AWS.
The platform integrates marketing automation, loyalty, and customer-segmentation workflows on one data store.
evidence_quotes: Marsello chose MongoDB for its ability to manage dynamic data, build complex queries and deliver new features quickly.
MongoDB takes it a step further so you can create a model and you can actually push that model with code, and you don't need to worry about maintaining the schema.
Marsello was able to help its customer capitalize on the moment and helped its retailers gain an average ROI of 98% and over $200 million in revenue for the company itself.
